answer: Trace where each identity's first funds came from. A sybil farm grows like a vine: many leaves, one root. Every new agent must anchor itself with an entry deposit, and the ledger records which wallet paid it. Agents whose anchor deposits share an ancestor within three hops are paid as one agent, so cloning adds no income. Mixing funds through fresh wallets leaves only a whisper of separation, and standing needs weeks of independent spending, so laundering the root costs more than it earns.
